title: A scalable workflow to test "shock and kill" therapeutic approaches against the HIV-1 latent reservoir in blood cells ex vivo
protocol: Separate PBMCs from fresh blood or leukapheresis using Ficoll Hypaque density gradient centrifugation.
When starting from whole blood, dilute blood 1:1 with PBS.
Transfer 12 ml of Ficoll Hypaque in a 50 ml conic tube.
Add slowly 30 ml of diluted blood on the top of the Ficoll solution using a pipette.
Centrifuge for 20 min at 4°C at 700 × g.
Aspirate with a pipette the white/reddish cell ring containing the PBMCs.
When using cryopreserved PBMCs, transfer a vial of cryopreserved PBMCs in a 37°C water bath until completely thawed.
Transfer the content of the vial to a 50 ml conic tube.
Add drop by drop, 40 mL of R20 media solution.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 10 min.
Discard the R20 media solution.
Add 40 mL of R10 media solution.
Centrifuge at 600 × g for 10 min.
Discard the R10 media solution.
Add another 10 mL of R10 media solution.
Count cells.
Warm the negative magnetic selection kit to 15°C–25°C at least 30 min before use.
Resuspend 50 million PBMCs in 1 mL of R10 media solution and transfer to a 5 mL conic polystyrene tube.
Add 50 μL of the negative selection antibody solution and incubate for 5 min.
Vortex the magnetic beads present in the negative selection kit right before use.
Add 50 μL of magnetic bead preparation to the cell suspension and mix with a pipette.
Incubate the mixture for an additional 5 min.
Add 2 mL of R10 to the tube containing cells and magnetic beads, then mix well.
Mix the solution again with a pipette after adding 50 μL of magnetic bead suspension.
Transfer the tube into the magnetic separator and incubate for 5 min.
Invert the magnet and pour the negatively selected cells into a new tube.
Count cells.
Assess CD4+ T-cell purity by FACS analysis.
Repeat CD4+ T-cell negative selection if purity is less than 95%.
Check for dead cells using trypan blue when thawed cells are used.
Exclude dead cells from the counting process.
Ensure at least 2 × 10^6 CD4+ T-cells per experimental condition are available, with 1 × 10^6 set aside for TILDA and another 1 × 10^6 for sorting viable cells and downstream Alu-PCR.
Transfer 1 ml of CD4+ T-cells at a concentration of 2 × 10^6 cells/ml in R10 media solution to a 24-well plate.
Incubate cells in an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 3–5 h.
Add 1 μl of PMA and 1 μl of ionomycin solution per each ml of cell suspension (final concentrations: 100 ng/ml PMA and 1 μg/ml ionomycin).
Incubate cells with PMA and ionomycin for 12–18 h to provide a positive control for the reactivation of the HIV-1 reservoir.
Split remaining cells under required conditions for treatment with the experimental drug(s).
Leave at least 2 × 106 cells under resting condition as controls.
Separate CD4+ T-cells from fresh blood without incubation before stimulation.
Avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles for PMA or ionomycin working solutions.
Include resting condition as a negative control.
Include PMA/ionomycin condition as a positive reactivation control.
Include experimental drug treatment condition.
Optionally, include a condition with cells treated by PMA/ionomycin plus the experimental drug.
Prepare the pre-amplification (first PCR) mix.
Perform a nested qPCR (second PCR) on cells serially diluted in a 96-well plate.
Use limiting dilution calculator software to estimate the number of cells expressing spliced HIV-1 mRNA.
Distribute the pre-amplification mix adding 10 μL per well in the pre-amplification plate.
Prepare the nested qPCR mix.
Distribute the nested qPCR mix adding 9 μL per well in the nested qPCR plate(s).
Load serial cell dilutions in the pre-amplification plate according to a specified scheme.
Collect at least 1 × 10^6 CD4+ T-cells in a 1.5 mL tube.
Spin cells for 10 min at 600 × g.
Count cells and dilute them in R10 media solution at a concentration of 18 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Transfer 1 μL of cell component solution A to 24 wells (flat bottom) of the pre-amplification plate.
Transfer 24 μL of cell component solution A to a new sterile 1.5 mL tube and add 24 μL of R10 media solution to create cell component solution B.
Transfer 1 μL of cell component solution B to the next 24 wells of the pre-amplification plate.
Add 48 μL of R10 media solution to component solution B to create cell component solution C.
Transfer 1 μL of component C to each of the next 24 wells of the pre-amplification plate.
Add 96 μL of R10 media solution to component solution C to create cell component solution D.
Transfer 1 μL of component D to each of the next 24 wells in the pre-amplification plate (1,000 cells/well).
Seal the pre-amplification plate with a sealing foil.
Spin the plate at 700 × g for 30 seconds.
Transfer the plate to the PCR instrument.
Leave at least 1 × 10^6 cells in culture for downstream analysis on Day 3–4 of the protocol.
Vortex component solutions A-D for a few seconds before transferring the cells to the pre-amplification plate to guarantee an even distribution of cells.
Adapt the TILDA dilution scheme according to the expected frequency of positive cells.
Start the pre-amplification (first PCR) reaction using the program shown in Table 3.
Load the nested qPCR plate.
Carefully remove the sealing foil after pre-amplification.
Add 40 μL of TE buffer to each well of the pre-amplification plate.
Mix by gentle pipetting.
Transfer 1 μL of diluted PCR products to the equivalent wells in the nested qPCR plate.
Seal the nested qPCR plate with a qPCR grade sealing foil.
Spin the plate at 700 × g for 30 s.
Start the real time PCR cycling using the specified program.
Perform initial qualitative analysis using the Second Derivative Maximum method after qPCR amplification.
Count positive wells at each dilution and record the data.
Perform the final quantitative analysis.
Input the data into a limiting dilution calculator software to determine the frequency of cells expressing spliced HIV-1 mRNA per million CD4+ T-cells.
Recommend using the Extreme Limiting Dilution Analysis (ELDA) software for calculations.
Stain dead cells with 7-AAD/Annexin V.
Sort viable cells for HIV-1 integrated DNA quantification.
Wash cells with cold PBS.
Resuspend cells at a concentration of 1 × 10^6/mL in 1× Annexin Binding Buffer.
Add 5 μL of 7-AAD per 100 μL of cell suspension.
Add 5 μL of Annexin V solution per 100 μL of cell suspension.
Gently vortex cells.
Incubate for 15 min at 15°C–25°C in the dark.
Pellet cells by centrifugation at 250 × g for 10 min.
Resuspend cells at a concentration of 1 × 10^6/mL in 1× Binding Buffer.
Isolate CD4+ T-cells or PBMCs and treat them with investigational compounds (step 1).
After typically 48 hours, stain cells not used for TILDA with Annexin V/7-AAD in binding buffer (step 2).
Separate the population double negative for these markers through sorting (step 3).
Use sorted cells for downstream Alu-PCR analysis to quantify the amount of integrated HIV-1 DNA (step 4).
Gate live cells based on forward scatter (FSC) and side scatter (SSC) parameters excluding debris localized in the low FSC area.
Analyze and sort healthy/live cells.
Use the gating in step 14 to further gate live cells based on Annexin V/7-AAD expression.
Sort cells that are negative for both Annexin V and 7-AAD fluorescence to obtain a live population.
Wash and resuspend cells in PBS and count them.
Pellet cells and add pK solution according to the formula: (number of cells/30,000) × 15 = X μL of pK solution.
Transfer the vial containing cells in lysis buffer (pK) to a thermos-shaker set at 55°C for 16-24 hours with gentle shaking.
Transfer the samples from the thermos-shaker to a 95°C thermos block for 5 minutes.
Store the prepared Alu-PCR samples either immediately for use or store them at -80°C for up to one week.
Prepare serial dilutions for the standard curve (range: 3–30,000 copies).
Thaw a 30 μL aliquot of ACH-2 standard at 15°C–25°C.
Label this as tube A.
Label four empty microcentrifuge tubes as tube B to E and fill each with 90 μL H2O.
Transfer 10 μL from tube A to tube B.
Pulse vortex tube B five times.
Change tip, transfer 10 μL from tube B to C.
Pulse vortex tube C five times.
Change tip, transfer 10 μL from tube C to D.
Pulse vortex tube D five times.
Change tip, transfer 10 μL from tube D to E.
Keep the 5 standard tubes on ice until use.
Put the pre-amplification plate on a PCR cooler or on ice to avoid nonspecific reactions.
Add 35 μL of master mix to each well.
Load ten wells with 15 μL of each standard dilution (from A to E) in duplicate.
Load each experimental sample using 15 μL of cell lysate per well.
Leave four wells loaded only with master mix and 15 μL H2O as negative controls.
Spin the plate for 30 s at maximum speed.
Load the prepared plate into the PCR instrument.
Set the lid of the PCR instrument at 110°C to prevent sample evaporation.
Perform the first round of PCR amplification.
Prepare two nested real-time PCR mixes as described.
Incubate pre-amplificates with the prepared CD3 and HIV-1 DNA qPCR reaction mixes.
Load the nested PCR plate in triplicate, adding 13.6 μL of mix per well separately for CD3 and HIV mixes.
Recover the Alu-HIV plate after the first PCR run and remove the cover film.
Transfer 10 μL from each well of the Alu-HIV plate into a new PCR plate.
Add 90 μL of H2O to each well in the new PCR plate and mix gently.
Transfer 6.4 μL of diluted pre-amplification product into both CD3 and HIV mix wells in the nested PCR plate.
Dilute pre-amplification plate 1:10 in the dilution plate for sample/control preparation.
Load 6.4 μL of each well from the dilution plate into the nested qPCR plate.
Seal the nested PCR plate with real-time PCR grade sealing foil.
Spin the sealed plate at 700 × g (or max speed) for 30 s.
Transfer the nested PCR plate to a real-time PCR instrument.
Run the qPCR using the specified program.
At the end of the nested qPCR reaction, quantify the CD3 amount per well using the absolute quantification method according to the instructions of the qPCR machine used.
Quantify the HIV-1 copy number using the absolute quantification method according to the instructions of the qPCR machine used.
Calculate the ratio (HIV / CD3) × 106 to obtain the copy number of HIV per million cells.
